findings.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupAdapter.java (~266-270): The fix is incomplete — only getSubGroupsCount() got the null guard, but the adjacent getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (and any other getGroupModel() delegation) still NPEs when modelSupplier returns null under the same concurrent-deletion race, reachable via the admin children endpoint with search/first/max (the GroupUtils.toRepresentation path with populateSubGroups), so the PR's stated goal is only partially met.

[Medium/api] GroupAdapter.java (274-275): getSubGroupsCount() can now return null where it previously returned a count or failed, silently changing the method's contract; callers that unbox the Long or aggregate it into null-intolerant structures (e.g., REST endpoints building Map<String, Long> counts via Collectors.toMap/Map.of, which throw NPE on null values) will now fail elsewhere — the failure is relocated rather than handled. A typed 'group no longer exists' exception, or filtering stale entries at the cache/listing layer, would be safer.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti (~133-153): The reader thread is never join()ed, so assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) can execute while the reader is still mid-request; an exception caused by the race can be recorded after the assertion (false pass), and the thread may still be issuing requests when the test method/teardown completes.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java (~148-151): deletedAll is set only on the happy path (no try/finally); if any remove() in the deletion loop throws, the reader thread's sole exit condition is never met and it spins indefinitely hammering the server, hanging or destabilizing the rest of the suite.

[Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java (~131-147): Nothing verifies that reads actually overlapped the deletion window (no read counter, latch, or barrier), so depending on thread scheduling the test can pass without ever exercising the concurrent scenario it is meant to guard.

[Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java (~140): The test only exercises the brief-representation listing path (groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) → getSubGroupsCount()); the sub-group search/tree path that remains vulnerable is not covered, so a regression there would go undetected.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new null-guard only in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` by calling `modelSupplier.get()` directly and returning `null` if it is `null`. No analogous change is shown for other `GroupAdapter` methods (e.g., the nearby `getSubGroupsStream(...)` appears unchanged in this hunk), so if `modelSupplier` can indeed return `null` during concurrent deletion, the fix may be incomplete. However, the diff does not show `getSubGroupsStream(...)`’s body nor `getGroupModel()`’s behavior, so an actual NPE is not directly verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java (~148-151): deletedAll is set only on the happy path (no try/finally); if any remove() in the deletion loop throws, the reader thread's sole exit condition is never met and it spins indefinitely hammering the server, hanging or destabilizing the rest of the suite.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, the reader thread loops on `while (!deletedAll.get())` and `deletedAll.set(true)` is executed only after the deletion loop. If any `managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, the method exits early and `deletedAll` is never set, leaving a non-daemon thread spinning indefinitely and potentially hanging/destabilizing the test suite. There is no `try/finally` or thread join/interrupt to ensure shutdown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java (~131-147): Nothing verifies that reads actually overlapped the deletion window (no read counter, latch, or barrier), so depending on thread scheduling the test can pass without ever exercising the concurrent scenario it is meant to guard.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, the reader thread is started and immediately the main thread proceeds to delete all groups and then sets `deletedAll` to true. There is no latch/barrier/counter ensuring the reader loop actually executed while deletions were happening (or even executed at all) before `deletedAll` flips. Therefore the test can pass without exercising the intended concurrent read-vs-delete scenario, making the finding accurate and actionable but not a product bug.

adjudication.rationale: The added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` indeed only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` (brief listing), but the finding’s claim that a specific “sub-group search/tree path … remains vulnerable” is not verifiable from this diff: no search/tree logic is changed here, and the diff does not show any remaining vulnerability or an uncovered new code path beyond `getSubGroupsCount()`’s null-guard change.
